result:
The count comes to 17, which I derived by hand; I did not check it by brute force.

**Setup.** Call a pair "friends" if they are friends or frenemies, and "enemies" if they are enemies or frenemies. Rule 1 says the friendship relation is transitive, so it splits the five people into friend classes. Any two people in different classes are enemies only (not friends).

**At most two classes.** Suppose three classes had one person each, A, B, C. Then A–B and B–C are enemy pairs, so rule 2 makes A and C friends. That contradicts them being in different classes, so there are at most two classes.

**Case 1: no frenemies.**
- All five are in one class, and everyone is friends: 1 configuration.
- There are two nonempty classes, with friends inside each class and enemies across: (2⁵ − 2)/2 = 15 configurations.

These 16 are the 2-colorings of the five people up to swapping the colors.

**Case 2: some frenemy pair a, b.**
1. Suppose a person x is in another class. Then x–a and x–b are enemy-only pairs. Since a and b are enemies, rule 2 applied to x–a and a–b makes x and b friends. That contradicts x being in a different class, so everyone is in one class.
2. Take any c in the class. Rule 3 applied to c–a (friends) and a–b (enemies) makes c and b enemies. By the same argument, every pair is enemies, and every pair is also friends, so all pairs are frenemies.
3. All pairs being frenemies satisfies all three rules, so this gives 1 configuration.

**Total.** 16 + 1 = 17.

ANSWER: 17
